newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat falls to fresh three-year lows, harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat falls to fresh three-year lows, harvest.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures fell to a fresh three-year low for a nearby contract on aggressive combining of the U.S. winter wheat crop plus persistent reports of excellent yields, traders said.
"Yields have been very good in the winter areas and the showers will help the spring wheat," said Tom Levis, analyst for Prudential Securities.

There were some forecasts for rain this week in the U.S. Plains states which would slow combining in the hard red winter growing region. But traders and analysts said the rain would boost spring wheat prospects.

Contract lows were set in nearly every month and new crop July fell to a session low of $3.13 per bushel, a new three-year low for a nearby contract. The previous contract low of $3.19-1/2 per bushel was set a week ago.
Nearly ideal harvest weather was reported over the weekend and the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop apparently will be ample, with widespread talk of better-than-expected yields per acre.
CBOT soft red winter wheat closed unchanged to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 6-3/4 at $3.13-1/2. September was down 5-3/4 at $3.21-3/4.

A KCBT trader of hard red winter wheat on Monday said there was so much HRW wheat being combined that wheat feeding may be commonplace this year. KCBT hard red winter wheat futures also sank to contract lows in early dealings.
Also there have been reports of excellent soft red winter wheat crop yields.

Export news failed to generate support with USDA Monday pegging U.S. wheat export inspections during the week ended July 3 at 14.025 million bushels, near the low end of estimates which ranged from 12 million to 20 million bushels.
Cargill Inc sold three million bushels September, traders said, and LIT America bought one million bushels of September.
In spread trading, SAK Futures did one half million bushels September/July at eight cents, premium September, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 22,423 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Paine Webber sold 150 September $4.00 puts at 75 to 78 cents and E.D. and F. Man International bought 400 December $3.60 calls at 9-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, above the 5,181 traded Thursday.
